title: Hierarchical staging and rate-adaptive retirement plan for embedding models
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: New embedding models and quantized variants are arriving more frequently, and our current single-stage canary process is causing either long tails in deprecations or abrupt customer-impacting regressions. We need a repeatable, tenant-aware staging flow that: 1) separates 'hot-path' low-latency traffic from 'warm' bulk inference, 2) exercises quantized and float variants in parallel without violating latency SLOs, and 3) provides a predictable, metrics-driven retirement schedule for old variants.
acceptance_criteria: Staging pipeline supports hierarchical traffic splits: hot-path vs warm-path routing per tenant
Rate-adaptive retirement policy implemented and configurable per model alias
Telemetry captures drift and quality fences: recall@10 regression, embedding L2 drift, p95 latency, and error rate
Automated smoke-eval harness runs on shadow traffic and produces pass/fail signal for rollout gates
Runbook updated and linked; at least one internal canary completed with zero customer-facing degradations
steps: Design hierarchical split: default 80% hot-path (low latency) / 20% warm-path (batch-friendly) — adjustable per tenant
Implement per-tenant routing flags and traffic shaping in gateway (small config + feature flag)
Add variant tagging: float32, int8-q, int8-q-hf (hot-fast), and lightweight-reranker variants
Build shadow-eval pipeline to mirror warm-path traffic to new variant pool and run semantic regression tests
Instrument telemetry (Grafana dashboard + alert): p50/p95/p99 latency, recall@10 change, embedding norm drift, and CPU/GPU utilization
Create rate-adaptive retirement controller: policy defines decay curve and tenant opt-out windows
Run closed internal pilot with 3 tenants (support, docs, platform) and iterate based on telemetry
Produce runbook and incident playbook; train SREs and Solutions Engineers
comments: 2025-01-20: Spike complete. Proof-of-concept for hot/warm split implemented in embed-gateway branch (GH: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1876). Baseline tests show warm-path batching reduces token cost by ~28% for bulk vectorization jobs.
2025-01-24: Design review with PM and Design. Decided to keep default hot/warm ratio conservative (80/20) to protect latency-sensitive tenants. Action: add tenant-level override for experiments.

2025-01-29: Telemetry schema proposed. Added signals for embedding L2 norm drift and cosine-distance-based semantic recall. Draft Grafana dashboard at https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/embeddings/hierarchical-staging (internal).
2025-02-01: Security review request filed (DOC: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/Embed+Staging). Security sign-off not required for initial pilot; will be required for org-wide rollout.
2025-02-02: PR opened for rate-adaptive retirement controller (GH: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2324). Looking for infra + SRE reviewers. Luca to lead pilot coordination.
notes: Trade-offs: more complex routing increases configuration surface and debugging cost. Mitigation: provide curated defaults and single toggle to revert to legacy path.
Decision: warm-path will accept slightly higher latency but must maintain recall@10 within -1.5% relative to float baseline during pilot.
Fallback policy: if semantic regression > threshold OR p95 latency for hot-path > 1.25x baseline, auto-fallback to pinned variant and page SRE
Open question: whether to expose retirement decay curves to customers or keep as platform-managed — proposed platform-managed for first 2 quarters
